subject: gr-qc
title_original: Lecture notes: Introduction to the Off-shell Double Copy Program
abstract: The present notes are based on a series of lectures prepared for an introductory eight-class course on the modern framework of the off-shell double copy. The course was held from April 16 to May 4, 2026, at Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA). These lectures, aimed at PhD and master's students, are self-contained and require only a basic knowledge of classical field theory. The main goal is to review the fundamental concepts of gauge and gravitational theories in order to explore the off-shell frameworks of the single and double copy. In the final part of the course, we explore modern approaches to reinterpreting the single and double copy within T-duality-invariant frameworks.
title_relatable: How do you build gravity by squaring a simpler force?
hook: Lecture notes explain how gravity theories can be constructed by 'squaring' gauge theories, even away from physical particle trajectories.
summary: These course notes walk through the idea that gravity is, in a precise mathematical sense, the square of a gauge theory like electromagnetism — a relationship called the double copy. The notes cover both on-shell and off-shell versions of this correspondence, ending with how it fits inside T-duality-invariant frameworks. Aimed at graduate students, they're a self-contained entry point to a technique increasingly used to simplify gravitational wave calculations.
